audit.why: 53.45% over 2131 games — the largest sample in this slice — sits close enough to even that 5.5/10 with Locke carry 6/10 reads fairly, and the chart gives Locke only the first-item row.

Both layers read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Locke/Skill, matching packet.levelChart row for row, and the phases[] whys already name the reason each stage sits where it does (Purgatory at 6, Lich Bane at first item, execute scaling falling off at two items). No mirror exists yet for locke__sylas.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's defect line — no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere — is accurate: the page repeatedly says 'punish the ten seconds after each spent blink' and 'commit on the post-E window' without ever stating a single cooldown. Separately, Soul Ignition's true damage is never mentioned while itemization recommends MR.
audit.why: Kit: Q 10/9/8/7/6s at 950 range; Soul Ignition W 18/17/16/15/14s, deals TRUE damage and self-damages then refunds a portion as healing; Ashen Pursuit E a flat 10s with an auto-attack reset; Purgatory R 120/100/80s with grounding, slow and an execute.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries the Q, E and R numbers; report[8] states the true damage; dontsFull[0].d names the auto reset.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] says 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal', and recommends MR against a kit whose W deals true damage. Both are wrong, and the anti-heal line is a negative statement the relevance rule would exclude even if it were right.
audit.why: Grievous Wounds reduces all healing received, including a self-refund; the _missing file lists needs-antiheal on Soul Ignition specifically. And resistances-invalidated is listed on the same ability, so MR is the wrong purchase against the damage that matters.
audit.corrected: Itemization now buys Grievous Wounds for the W refund and drops the MR recommendation, keeping the Zhonya's-beats-the-execute line intact.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats the blink as the burst cue.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule autoreset-burst-tell: Ashen Pursuit carries an auto reset, so the attack wind-up after the dash is the real tell.

edits.before: - Locke Ritual Nails (Marks): matchup-defining — The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Track it before every step-up. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): his ONLY mobility, resets on takedowns — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): never fight at sliver HP inside the zone.
edits.after: - Locke Ritual Nails (Marks): matchup-defining — the marks are his whole engine, and the Q is 10/9/8/7/6s; without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents, so sidestep the recasts and punish the gap. Track it before every step-up. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): a flat 10s and his ONLY mobility, resets on takedowns — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): 120/100/80s; never fight at sliver HP inside the zone.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.
edits.after: Early HP blunts the nail chip, but MR will not: Soul Ignition deals true damage. A Zhonya's-class answer beats Purgatory outright — untargetable at the floor means execute denied. Bring Grievous Wounds for his W refund.

edits.before: That is Locke’s favourite window — refusing it removes half his win condition.
edits.after: His E is an auto reset — the attack wind-up is the cue, not the blink.

notes: Two things I could not fix inside a per-field edit. (1) The full layer calls Locke's Q 'Ritual Nails' in nine places (tldr, winCon, enemyWin, loading, focus.text, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[2].d, report[3], report[5]); Riot's own description in the kit reads 'Locke readies a set of Soul Nails to throw', and the _missing file names his W 'Soul Ignition' and his E 'Ashen Pursuit' — so 'Ritual Nails' looks like the same class of fabrication as 'Noxious Blight'. It needs a champion-level rename, not nine independent band-fitted rewrites. (2) tldr, report[0], breakdown.early and breakdown.wave build the whole plan on Locke being a '125-range' champion you out-range — but his Q is 950 and Sylas's is 775, so he out-ranges you with the ability that actually trades. The advice 'win the lane at range' is backwards. Both are raised in questionsForUser.
